I feel sorry for him now, I am thinking to call him and tell him that actual issue was my pc adaptor

articles.title: Weather on the board today
articles.body:
A dense fog of skin tone insecurity settled over the board at dawn, triggered by a request for an AI gender swap.

The drizzle persisted through the morning, thick with insults and a persistent high-pressure system of caste anxiety that refused to break. By midday, the sky cleared briefly into a dry, intellectual haze.

Anon debated space determinism and agrarian pessimism, a cold snap of geopolitical dread that offered little warmth.

This was followed by a sudden gust of border control anger, a brief but sharp squall of dataposts regarding intelligence agency staffing and breeding.

The evening brought a mixed front: a low-lying mist of claimed demographic shifts sat over the notices section, while a localized drought of technical frustration churned in the bottom right.

For one anon, a week of router complaints turned out to be a single-band adaptor, a micro-climate of relief that ended the week's static.

articles.title: Anon Requests AI Gender Swap, Receives Insults About Skin Tone
articles.body:
An anons posted a selfie on /b/ and asked Gemini to generate a female version of his own face.

The post invited the board to judge the result with the standard "smash or pass" query, framing the AI output as a test of his underlying attractiveness. The immediate response was hostile.

One respondent claimed that only "gobar kalus" engage in such activities, arguing that the OP had feminine tendencies but looked too "abbo" to express them without the aid of AI and numerous filters.

This user labeled the OP as "Uggo pro max," suggesting the digital alteration was necessary to mask an unappealing physical reality. Another user pointed out that AI tends to smooth skin excessively, noting that the generated image did not reflect the OP's true appearance.

This anon suggested that if the AI were asked to recreate the image with less filtering, it might produce a "7/10 chadlet," implying the original photo was heavily edited to hide flaws.

A third participant agreed that the AI would not give accurate results because the OP already used hundreds of filters to make himself look fairer and smoother. The thread quickly devolved into ethnic and sexual slurs.

One user called the OP a "pajeet" and suggested reverse-engineering his ID to prove he was a "gobarjeeta." Another asked how life was treating "Aditya Gobardas Dan." In response to the accusations, one anon insisted they were a "pyaari" and not a "gobar," while another dismissed the critics as "shitskin kaalu" and told them to keep coping.

Further replies included requests for the AI to generate a "nigress" version, a "Jew" version, and a "male version" of the female AI image.

One user posted a caption reading "Me if I were a gorimem." The antagonism continued with one anon calling the OP a "faggot ass tranny" and another labeling him a "bhangi." The thread ended with a user exclaiming "Ye to gobar hai yaar," reinforcing the consensus that the OP was attempting to use AI to escape his perceived physical and ethnic identity.

The board treated the request not as a technical curiosity, but as a confession of insecurity requiring immediate mockery.

articles.title: Space Determinism and Agrarian Pessimism
articles.body:
Anon declared that space will define the fate of nations for the next three hundred years. The thread immediately fractured into a debate over whether that claim was intelligent or absurd, with accusations of low IQ flying within minutes.

One respondent rejected the premise entirely, stating that there is nothing out there and that Earth is the only celestial body with living beings. This anon argued that the planet already provides everything necessary for a sustainable life.

They predicted that in three hundred years, only agrarian societies will survive while the rest will perish.

Another anon labeled the OP a 70 IQ case, while a third countered that the 70 IQ remark applied to the original poster's statement, not the agrarian prediction. Proponents of the space argument pointed to American technology.

One anon claimed the US is light years ahead and has its own AI. Another noted that they built AI and have a flag on the moon.

A third insisted the US Space Force actually exists and that their uniforms are real. An opposing voice corrected the usage of "light years," noting it is a measure of distance, not time.

A defender of the phrase called the correction an act of stupidity, claiming it was a pun on space travel. The discussion devolved into racial and physical slurs.

One anon described the OP as white and the respondent as a shitskinned pajeet, predicting the former would live in a developed country while the latter would die in a building collapse.

Another anon asked why a shudra jhaat was arguing the opposite of their kang. One poster simply wrote "Brutal" in response to the pile-on. The thread ended with dismissals and absurdity. One anon called the OP's statement AI slop.

Another asked for bio mass.

One poster said "yeah sure bud." Another simply replied, "Billions must die like literally." The argument over the fate of nations collapsed into a mix of scientific pedantry, ethnic insult, and disbelief at the scale of the original claim.

articles.title: Debates on Border Control and Intelligence Agency Staffing
articles.body:
Anon posted a derogatory graphic description of a woman, asking if she exemplified the nationalist tendencies of a specific demographic compared to Naxal sympathizers. One respondent countered by framing the situation as a severe national security failure.

He claimed a Pakistani woman entered India illegally with three children and was granted Scheduled Caste reservation by the government without any legal action being taken.

Another anon corrected the details, stating the woman was already the mother of four children from her previous marriage and had two more with a man named Sachin.

The discussion shifted to the competence of the Research and Analysis Wing. One poster argued that the agency hired Ravindra Kaushik, a stage actor from a rural village, without him passing any civil service examinations.

He claimed Kaushik penetrated the Pakistani Army. A rebuttal suggested the incident was a psyop and questioned what the Home Ministry was doing during the entry.

Critics of the R&AW described its staff as elderly individuals who rely on open-source intelligence and produce poor reports. They accused the agency of failing to curb cyber espionage and allowing foreign powers to compromise government computers.

One anon alleged that feed hijacking was used to induce psychosis in subjects. The thread also touched on the influence of the IPS lobby over paramilitary forces.

One poster mocked the R&AW chief for avoiding garlic and onions while collecting perks. Another claimed Operation Chindoor was halted after the United States intervened.

The conversation ended with accusations of mental illness and ethnic slurs directed at the original poster and his family. One anon called for the removal of the Home Minister, referencing his support for a specific political figure.

articles.title: Anon Claims Board Demographics
articles.body:
Anon posted that Indiachan /b/ had become a majority Muslim board and was deteriorating as a result. A respondent immediately rejected the premise, arguing the board remained a majority abbo space where Hindus attempted to bring others' names down.

Another reply proposed a specific theory: a single Muslim user, or a small group of two to three Hyderabadis, was creating abbo threads, seething on them, calling the OP a Muslim, and then complaining about Muslims ruining the board.

One poster countered this by noting that whoever claimed the OP was Muslim always cursed Allah. Others dismissed the Muslim presence entirely, stating there were no single Mohammedan on the site.

One user added that Dalits and Dravidians were historically excluded from Hinduism, while another blamed the government for being run by Gujjews.

articles.title: Single Band Adaptor Causes Week-Long Router Complaints
articles.body:
An anon admitted that a week of router complaints stemmed from a single-band PC wifi adaptor, not the router itself. After switching to a dual-band unit, connection and speed issues vanished.

The poster planned to call the installation technician again to apologize for five days of harassment.

One respondent mocked the spelling of "adaptor" as rural, while another noted that fiber is the actual internet backbone, not cellular towers.

A heated exchange followed where one anon claimed ethernet connections ultimately rely on cellular infrastructure. Others retorted with slurs and accusations of ignorance, demanding fiber-to-the-home for stable speeds.
